messages:
sophia_platform: Morning all — async checkin

What I did: pushed a rate-limit config tweak to the canary pool (PR: https://git.redwood/inference/pr/482). Verified route fallback behavior for /v1/generate when capacity drops.
Blockers: seeing sporadic 429s from the canary at traffic spikes (~200 rps). Suspect batching window math + prefix cache interactions. Need a quick pair to inspect kernel-selection metrics.
Today: will try a rollback of the quantized-llama variant on canary and run a diagnostic trace. Ping @alex_dev and @maya_infra for a quick sync in-thread.

alex_dev: saw the 429s last night, can join. quick note — the canary uses `max_batch_delay_ms: 12` right now, try increasing to `20` to smooth the bursts. Also pushed a tiny logging patch that surfaces batch sizes (PR: https://git.redwood/inference/pr/487).

maya_infra: I can bump the delay and run a staged load against canary, timeline ~30m. Also checked the auth tokens and KMS integrations — nothing anomalous there. :+1:

raj_ops: fyi deploy-bot flagged a failed deploy at 01:14 UTC, logs show `route_policy_evaluation timeout` in the canary healthcheck. Will paste logs into #incidents if someone wants them. If we increase batch delay, keep an eye on tail latency vs SLO.

deploy-bot: deploy job #682 failed: step 'canary-healthcheck' exited 1. See run: https://ci.redwood/runs/682

sophia_platform: thanks — if bumping `max_batch_delay_ms` doesn't stabilize, i'll open a short rollback and cut traffic by 30% to the stable pool. Also need an owner for a follow-up to tune `prefix_cache_ttl` for high-cardinality clients (we're seeing many small prefixes thrash the cache).

alex_dev: will review PR 487 in ~15m. I can own the `prefix_cache_ttl` follow-up and write a short RFC for cache sharding heuristics.

ci-bot: CI passed for PR 487 on main (build #221). :white_check_mark:

sophia_platform: great — coordinating rollback plan if needed. thanks everyone, will report back here with verification and perf numbers. :rocket:
